# Entity Merge Authority System — Design Document

> **For Claude:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task.

**Goal:** Provide a persistent, analyst-reviewable merge authority for all entity types, with a fast `apply-merges` command that rebuilds the graph without re-running OCR or LLM calls.

**Architecture:** YAML-based merge files per entity type, auto-generated as DRAFT during processing, reviewed and CONFIRMED by analyst. Two-level status system (file-level + entry-level). Dedupe never touches CONFIRMED entries. Graph is derived from existing `graph_data.json` + merge files (preserving LLM-enriched fields like verification tiers and confidence scores).

**Tech Stack:** Python, Pydantic, PyYAML, existing dedupe infrastructure

---

## File Structure

```
cases/CASE-ID/
├── document_groups.yaml           # Already exists (multi-part document grouping)
├── entity_groups/
│   ├── person_groups.yaml         # Person entities + person-to-person relations
│   ├── property_groups.yaml       # Property entities + property-to-property relations
│   ├── organization_groups.yaml   # Org entities + org-to-org relations
│   ├── location_groups.yaml       # Location entities + location-to-location relations
│   └── cross_type_relations.yaml  # Cross-type relations (OWNS, CONFISCATED, etc.)
```

## YAML Format

### Entity Groups (e.g., `person_groups.yaml`)

```yaml
status: DRAFT                       # Top-level: DRAFT if any entry is DRAFT
extractions_hash: "a1b2c3d4e5f6"    # SHA-256 prefix of extractions dir at generation time

groups:
  - canonical_id: "person_mario_ceresa_001"
    canonical_name: "Mario Ceresa Rodríguez"
    status: CONFIRMED               # Per-group status
    members:
      - id: "person_mario_ceresa_001"
        name: "Mario Ceresa Rodríguez"
        source: dedupe
        confidence: 0.92
      - id: "person_mario_ceresa_047"
        name: "Mario Ceresa R."
        source: dedupe
        confidence: 0.87
      - id: "person_mario_feresa_012"
        name: "Mario Feresa"
        source: analyst             # Manually added by analyst
        confidence: 1.0

  - canonical_id: "person_juan_garcia_005"
    canonical_name: "Juan García"
    status: DRAFT                   # Not yet reviewed
    members:
      - id: "person_juan_garcia_005"
        name: "Juan García"
        source: dedupe
        confidence: 0.71
      - id: "person_juan_garsia_019"
        name: "Juan Garsia"
        source: dedupe
        confidence: 0.71

# Same-type relations (PARENT_OF, SPOUSE_OF, etc.)
relations:
  - source_id: "person_mario_ceresa_001"
    target_id: "person_juan_ceresa_002"
    relation_type: PARENT_OF
    date: null
    source: extraction
    status: CONFIRMED

unmerged:
  - id: "person_unknown_notary_088"
    name: "Unknown Notary"
```

### Cross-Type Relations (`cross_type_relations.yaml`)

```yaml
status: DRAFT
extractions_hash: "a1b2c3d4e5f6"

relations:
  - source_id: "person_mario_ceresa_001"
    target_id: "property_villa_aurelia_001"
    relation_type: OWNS
    date: "1952"
    source: dedupe
    status: CONFIRMED

  - source_id: "org_inra_001"
    target_id: "property_villa_aurelia_001"
    relation_type: CONFISCATED
    date: "1960"
    source: extraction
    status: DRAFT
```

## Two-Level Status System

| Top-level status | Meaning |
|-----------------|---------|
| `DRAFT` | File contains at least one DRAFT entry — needs analyst review |
| `CONFIRMED` | All entries reviewed — analyst has signed off |

| Per-entry status | Meaning |
|-----------------|---------|
| `DRAFT` | Auto-generated by dedupe/extraction, not yet reviewed |
| `CONFIRMED` | Analyst has verified this merge/relation |

**Rules:**
- Top-level is CONFIRMED only when every entry is CONFIRMED
- Adding new documents flips top-level back to DRAFT
- Dedupe never modifies CONFIRMED entries during re-processing
- Deleting an entry from the file undoes that merge on next `apply-merges`

## Constraints and Invariants

### Canonical ID Rules
- Canonical IDs are always existing entity IDs from extraction (never manually invented)
- The canonical is the **first member** of the group (the merge target)
- An entity ID may appear in **at most one group** across all files of the same type
- Validation rejects duplicate entity IDs across groups (hard error, not warning)

### Relation Rewriting
- When entities are merged, all relations pointing to a merged member are rewritten to the canonical ID
- Duplicate relations (same source, target, type) after rewriting are deduplicated, keeping the higher-confidence one
- Self-loops (source == target after rewriting) are dropped
- Bidirectional edges are preserved as separate relations (A→B and B→A remain distinct)

### Cross-Type Relations and DRAFT/CONFIRMED
- DRAFT relations are **skipped** by `apply-merges` by default
- DRAFT relations are **applied** only with `--include-drafts` flag (for preview)
- Same behavior as entity groups — analyst must CONFIRM before relations take effect

### LLM-Enriched Field Preservation
- `apply-merges` reads the current `graph_data.json`, not raw extractions
- Verification tiers, confidence scores, and all enriched fields are preserved
- When merging two entities, the canonical entity's fields take precedence; missing fields are filled from the merged member
- `extracted_from` is combined (comma-separated union of all source documents)

### Staleness Detection
- Each YAML file includes an `extractions_hash` header — SHA-256 of the extractions directory file listing at generation time
- `apply-merges` warns (but proceeds) if the hash doesn't match current extractions
- Stale files may reference entity IDs that no longer exist — these are logged as warnings and skipped

### Concurrency
- Single-analyst CLI workflow — no locking required for current scope
- Future: if multi-user Vault editing is added, implement file-level advisory locks

## Lifecycle

### First Processing

```
process CASE-ID
  → OCR, extraction, build raw graph
  → Run dedupe
  → Write entity_groups/*.yaml as DRAFT (all entries DRAFT)
  → Write cross_type_relations.yaml as DRAFT
  → Export graph_data.json (with dedupe merges applied)
  → Generate narrative
```

### Analyst Review

```
1. Open entity_groups/person_groups.yaml
2. Review each group:
   - Correct: leave as-is
   - Wrong merge: delete the member entry (or whole group)
   - Missing merge: add member with source: analyst, confidence: 1.0
3. Set each reviewed group's status to CONFIRMED
4. When all entries are CONFIRMED, set top-level status: CONFIRMED
5. Run: apply-merges CASE-ID
```

### Adding New Documents

```
process CASE-ID (with new documents)
  → OCR, extraction for new docs
  → Run dedupe (includes new entities)
  → Update entity_groups/*.yaml:
    - CONFIRMED entries: untouched
    - New dedupe clusters: added as DRAFT entries
    - Top-level status: flipped to DRAFT (new entries need review)
  → Apply CONFIRMED merges to graph
  → Export graph_data.json
  → Generate narrative
```

### Quick Fix (Manual Merge)

```bash
# Spot a bad split in the graph, merge from CLI
python3 -m farmer_factory.cli merge-entities CASE-ID entity_a entity_b

# This:
# 1. Adds entry to appropriate entity_groups/*.yaml
#    - source: analyst, status: CONFIRMED
# 2. Runs apply-merges automatically
```

### Undo a Merge

```
1. Open the relevant entity_groups/*.yaml
2. Delete the entry (or remove the member from a group)
3. Run: apply-merges CASE-ID
```

## CLI Commands

### `apply-merges` (new)

```bash
python3 -m farmer_factory.cli apply-merges CASE-ID --domain cuban_property
```

- Reads current `graph_data.json` + all CONFIRMED entity_groups/*.yaml files
- Rebuilds graph by merging entities and rewriting relations, preserving LLM-enriched fields
- **No OCR, no extraction, no LLM calls** — graph surgery only
- Idempotent — running twice produces same result
- Optional: `--include-drafts` to preview DRAFT merges without requiring CONFIRMED

### `merge-entities` (new)

```bash
python3 -m farmer_factory.cli merge-entities CASE-ID entity_id_a entity_id_b
```

- Writes merge entry to appropriate `entity_groups/*.yaml` with `source: analyst`, `status: CONFIRMED`
- Automatically runs `apply-merges`
- The canonical entity is the first argument (`entity_id_a`)

### `process` (modified)

Existing command gains merge file generation:
- After dedupe, writes/updates `entity_groups/*.yaml`
- Preserves CONFIRMED entries, adds new DRAFT entries
- Flips top-level status to DRAFT if new entries added

## Implementation Tasks

### Task 1: Pydantic Models for Merge Files

**Files:**
- Create: `farmer_factory/structure/merge_models.py`

Define models:
- `MergeGroupMember` — id, name, source (dedupe|analyst|extraction), confidence, status
- `MergeGroup` — canonical_id, canonical_name, status, members list
- `EntityGroupFile` — top-level status, groups list, relations list, unmerged list
- `CrossTypeRelation` — source_id, target_id, relation_type, date, source, status
- `CrossTypeRelationsFile` — top-level status, relations list

### Task 2: Merge File Writer

**Files:**
- Create: `farmer_factory/structure/merge_writer.py`

Write DRAFT merge files from dedupe results:
- `write_entity_groups(case_id, entity_type, dedupe_clusters, singletons)` — writes `entity_groups/{type}_groups.yaml`
- `write_cross_type_relations(case_id, relations)` — writes `cross_type_relations.yaml`
- Preserve existing CONFIRMED entries when updating
- Flip top-level status to DRAFT when adding new entries

### Task 3: Merge File Reader

**Files:**
- Create: `farmer_factory/structure/merge_reader.py`

Read and validate merge files:
- `read_entity_groups(case_id, entity_type)` → `EntityGroupFile`
- `read_cross_type_relations(case_id)` → `CrossTypeRelationsFile`
- `get_confirmed_merges(case_id)` → dict of all confirmed merge mappings
- Handle missing files gracefully (no merge files = no merges)

### Task 4: Apply-Merges Engine

**Files:**
- Create: `farmer_factory/structure/merge_engine.py`

Core graph rebuild logic:
- `apply_merges(case_id, include_drafts=False)` → writes `graph_data.json`
- Read current `graph_data.json` (preserves LLM-enriched fields)
- Build entity ID remapping from confirmed merge groups
- Merge entity nodes: canonical fields take precedence, combine `extracted_from`
- Rewrite all relations to use canonical IDs
- Deduplicate relations after rewriting (keep higher confidence)
- Drop self-loops created by merging
- Apply cross-type relation corrections from `cross_type_relations.yaml`
- Validate: warn on stale `extractions_hash`, skip references to missing entities
- Export merged graph

### Task 5: CLI Commands

**Files:**
- Modify: `farmer_factory/cli.py`

Add commands:
- `apply-merges CASE-ID --domain --include-drafts`
- `merge-entities CASE-ID entity_a entity_b`

### Task 6: Integrate with Process Pipeline

**Files:**
- Modify: `farmer_factory/processing/pipeline.py`
- Modify: `farmer_factory/structure/builder.py`

After dedupe runs:
- Call merge writer to generate/update DRAFT files
- Apply CONFIRMED merges before graph export

### Task 7: Unit Tests

**Files:**
- Create: `tests/structure/test_merge_models.py`
- Create: `tests/structure/test_merge_writer.py`
- Create: `tests/structure/test_merge_reader.py`
- Create: `tests/structure/test_merge_engine.py`

Test:
- YAML serialization/deserialization roundtrip
- CONFIRMED entries preserved on update
- Top-level status flips to DRAFT on new entries
- Merge application produces correct graph
- Idempotency of apply-merges
- merge-entities CLI writes correct YAML
- Entity ID appearing in multiple groups → validation error
- Relation rewriting with bidirectional edges (both preserved)
- Self-loop detection and removal after merge
- Duplicate relation deduplication (keep higher confidence)
- `--include-drafts` applies DRAFT entries, default skips them
- Stale `extractions_hash` produces warning but proceeds
- Missing entity IDs in merge file → logged warning, skipped
- Cross-type relations respect DRAFT/CONFIRMED status
